thread:
sam: deploy-bot just raised a rollback recommendation for story-render after we flipped the new streaming-friendly allocator. p95 doubled on hosted canary; deploy-bot suggests reverting hosted lanes only. change window ends 08:00 UTC. asking for manual approval so we can preserve a tenant test lane.
deploy-bot: ALERT: hosted canary story-render p95=940ms (baseline 360ms), error_rate 0.2% -> 1.9%. suggested rollback: v1.7.2. evidence: https://telemetry.redwood/canary/4732
anya: quick note: the change included allocator=stream-fast + feature flag:heavy_streaming. EU dedicated lanes are running a shadowed rollout (traffic-shadow) and must not be disturbed for migration tests. can we do a hosted-only revert?
tess: agree host-only rollback makes sense. we should also consider turning feature flag off while we investigate so we preserve traces. pinging @release-manager to coordinate the blurb and releaseboard note.
release-manager: i can flip the flag in feature-gate for hosted only: `feature-gate set heavy_streaming --env hosted --state off --reason "canary tails"` then kick targeted rollback. want both actions in the same maintenance window?
osps-runner: (ops-runner) small nit: deploy tooling needs the lane param. command example: `release rollback --svc story-render --to v1.7.2 --lane hosted --slice 10 --strategy rolling --reason "canary tail regression"`
sam: +1 to flip flag first, then revert. that reduces ripple and keeps the dedicated shadow lane intact. any SLA concerns?
csm: two customers have small hosted usage on the canary slice, i'll prepare a short note. recommend manual approval to avoid surprise auto-revert hitting dedicated tenants.
legal: cc. file an incident ticket if rollback executed; we'll review contract pins especially for dedicated migration customers.
release-manager: ok action plan: 1) flip heavy_streaming flag for hosted -> off, 2) suppress deploy-bot autorevert for 10m, 3) run hosted-only rollback to v1.7.2, 4) smoke + re-enable autoscale, 5) publish blurb. who executes?
osps-runner: i'll execute revert. assigning @tess to flip the flag and @anya to monitor shadowed lanes.
tess: flipping flag for hosted: `feature-gate set heavy_streaming --env hosted --state off` 
tess: flag flipped. waiting 30s for config propagation.
sam: suppressing autorevert: `deployctl suppress-autorevert --svc story-render --for 10m`
osps-runner: starting rollback now: ```release rollback --svc story-render --to v1.7.2 --lane hosted --slice 10 --strategy rolling --notes "manual: flag-off + preserve dedicated shadow"```
deploy-bot: ACTION: hosted rollback initiated by ops-runner. progress: 12% -> 48% -> 76% -> 100%.
anya: monitoring shadowed dedicated lane: p95 unchanged in shadow lane, no impact. hosted canary post-rollback p95=370ms, errors 0.25%. looks good.
release-manager: drafting customer blurb: "We detected a performance regression in a hosted canary and rolled back hosted to the previous stable version. Dedicated migration lanes were intentionally preserved. No customer data was affected. Engineering will follow up with an RCA." sending to CSM now.
csm: blurb received and being sent to affected customers. thanks for including the dedicated note.
legal: incident ticket INC-2026-4732 created. no immediate SLA breach indicated.
osps-runner: re-enabling autoscale on hosted canary: `infractl autoscale set story-hosted-canary --min 1 --max 6`
osps-runner: smoke checks run: latency and error budget within thresholds. 
sam: good. next steps: 1) publish releaseboard note (release-manager) 2) RCA owners? anya + infra. 3) monitor hosted for 2h (oncall).
anya: i'll own RCA. plan: compare allocator traces, kernel selection logs, and feature-flag pathing between hosted and dedicated shadow lane. target preliminary notes in 4 hours.
oncall-ops: monitoring rules tightened for hosted p95 for 2h. temporary alert set to 420ms.
sam: thanks everyone. hosted-only rollback and feature-flag unwind executed, dedicated shadow lane preserved, customers notified. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
